name: Mariehamn
title: Mariehamn Ship Gauging | UTM for Åland Ferries and Fleets
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Mariehamn for ro-pax ferries, cruise ships and Åland-managed tonnage: vehicle deck, tank, void and piping UTM between sailings.
h1: Hull Thickness Measurement for Ferries and Åland-Owned Ships in Mariehamn
intro: Mariehamn, the capital of the autonomous Åland Islands, is a shipowners' town as much as a port. Ferries linking Stockholm, Kapellskär, Turku, Helsinki and Tallinn call every day, and Åland companies manage ferries, tankers and cargo ships trading far beyond the islands. Calls here are short, so gauging is fitted into lay periods, or ordered by island-based superintendents for their ships wherever those ships dock. Atlantis has no one on Åland; the team is sent from India for each job.

highlights.h: Ferries that never leave the route
highlights.p: Ro-pax ferries calling at Mariehamn sail daily to fixed timetables. Gauging is broken into packages that fit a lay period or a gap in the schedule, with every visit completing its own set of spaces before the ship returns to service.

Many ships managed from Mariehamn seldom call there. Technical departments on the islands can commission gauging at whichever European port or yard their ship reaches next, with the team travelling from India to meet it on arrival.

Summer brings cruise calls and the busiest ferry timetables. The quieter months give operators more room to take a ship briefly out of rotation for maintenance, which is the better moment to open ballast tanks and voids for measurement.

port.h: Mariehamn's harbours and the Åland ferry trade
p: Mariehamn lies on a narrow peninsula in the south of mainland Åland, with water on both sides of the town. The Western Harbour is the deep-water side, where the passenger terminal and its ferry berths receive the ro-pax ships of Viking Line and Tallink Silja on routes connecting Stockholm and Kapellskär with Turku, Helsinki and Tallinn. The Eastern Harbour, across the town, is a sheltered small-craft and guest harbour rather than a commercial port. Approaches run through the islands and skerries of the Åland archipelago, so pilotage and careful navigation are part of every arrival. Some sailings between Turku and Stockholm stop at Långnäs on the eastern side of Åland rather than at Mariehamn, which spreads island traffic between two harbours.

What makes Mariehamn unusual is that Åland lies inside the EU but outside its VAT and excise territory, and that tax border is the reason so many Baltic ferries stop here: a call in Åland allows tax-free sales on board on routes that would otherwise run wholly inside the EU tax area. The islands also have wide self-government and a demilitarised status under international agreements. Shipping has been central to the economy for generations, from the sailing ships of the grain trade, remembered by the museum barque Pommern in the Western Harbour, to today's ferry companies and shipowners. Viking Line is headquartered in Mariehamn, and other Åland owners run tankers, ro-ro and cargo ships on international trades, many of which never come near the islands.

For a gauging team, Mariehamn offers two kinds of work. Ferries call several times a day but stay only briefly, so meaningful work aboard needs a lay period, a gap in the timetable or a technical stop, and ice-classed hulls on these routes wear at the waterline after each winter because the archipelago fairways ice over in most years. The second kind starts in Mariehamn but happens elsewhere: technical departments on the islands manage ships trading across Europe and beyond, and their superintendents commission gauging for dockings, surveys and sales wherever those ships happen to be. Cargo traffic at Mariehamn itself is modest and mostly serves the islands' own needs, carried by small cargo ships and the freight decks of the ferries.

At the Western Harbour ferry berths, work aboard a ro-pax depends on the ship being out of service for long enough: a planned lay day, a gap in the timetable or a technical stop. In those windows we measure vehicle-deck plating and stiffeners, scuppers and drain lines, voids and ballast tanks the crew has ventilated and certified, and piping in the engine room. Passenger safety rules and the ship's own procedures decide where the team may work while passengers are aboard, so most deck work is done with the car decks empty and closed to traffic.

There is no merchant dry dock on Åland, and the islands' ferries and cargo ships dock at mainland yards: Turku Repair Yard at Naantali, the shipyard at Rauma, which has docked Baltic ferries in recent years, or yards in Sweden, Poland and the Baltic states. For an Åland owner, the sensible approach is to collect deck, tank and piping readings during service calls and finish the bottom and remaining spaces in the dock, so the docking specification rests on measurement. Cargo ships at the port's freight berths can be gauged alongside while they discharge.
list: Western Harbour ferry berths — vehicle decks, voids, ballast tanks and engine-room piping on ro-pax during lay periods
Passenger terminal berths in summer — cruise ships and island cruises, with short scopes agreed with the ship in advance
Freight berths — alongside gauging on cargo ships supplying the islands, during discharge
Anchorage in the approaches — launch transfers to ships waiting off Mariehamn, weather and ice permitting
Mainland and Baltic docking yards — where Åland-managed ships complete the bottom and full tank programme
Ports and yards across Europe — gauging commissioned from Mariehamn for Åland-managed ships trading elsewhere

context.h: Åland's special status, port state control and ferry regulation
p: Port state control in Mariehamn is carried out by Traficom, the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency, under the Paris MoU, exactly as in other Finnish ports; Åland's autonomy covers many domestic matters but does not create a separate inspection regime for foreign ships. Passenger ships on the island routes are surveyed every year for their safety certificates, so structural findings on a ferry rarely wait long before someone asks about them. Because Åland remains part of the EU, voyages to and from Mariehamn count under the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime like other intra-EU legs, and ships of 500 gross tonnage and above carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation.

Ice and ageing tonnage shape the technical side. Ferries serving Mariehamn hold Finnish-Swedish ice classes, and seasons of archipelago ice abrade the bow, the shoulders and the waterline band, while constant berthing wears fender lines and stern areas. Several ships on the Åland routes have served for decades, and their owners weigh steel renewal against replacement under the pressure of the EU climate rules. That decision rests on condition data: vehicle-deck plating, ballast tanks, voids and the ice belt measured consistently from one docking to the next. Åland-owned tankers and cargo ships trading elsewhere bring the usual ESP and renewal-survey requirements, which their superintendents plan from Mariehamn.

jobs.p: Work linked to Mariehamn falls into two groups. On the ferries that call here, owners need renewal-survey and intermediate-survey gauging that the timetable will not allow in a single visit, so scopes are packaged into lay periods and completed in the annual docking. For ships managed by Åland companies but trading elsewhere, superintendents in Mariehamn order pre-docking estimates, owner's condition gauging and pre-purchase work at the ship's next port or yard. In both cases the plan is agreed with the technical department before the team leaves India, so the visit is spent on measurement rather than on finding access or waiting for tanks.
list: Vehicle-deck plating, scuppers and drain lines on a ro-pax at the Western Harbour, measured during a timetable gap
Ballast tanks and voids on a cruise ferry, gauged in packages across lay periods before its docking at a mainland yard
Ice-belt readings from inside the bow spaces of an ice-class ferry at the end of the winter
Pre-docking steel estimate on an Åland-managed product tanker at a European discharge port, commissioned from Mariehamn
Pre-purchase gauging for an Åland buyer of a second-hand ro-ro, carried out wherever the ship is lying

logistics: Mariehamn has its own airport with flights to the Finnish and Swedish mainland, and the islands are also reached by the same ferries the team may be gauging, from Turku, Helsinki or Stockholm. Long-haul arrivals from India usually come through Helsinki-Vantaa or Stockholm Arlanda. Ferry berths and passenger areas are controlled, so the ship's agent or operator arranges passes and the timing of access. Finland and Sweden are both Schengen states, and our technicians need a Schengen visa before travelling; we plan dates around the lay period once the operator confirms it.

General cargo ships supplying the islands

faqs.q: Can a ferry calling at Mariehamn be gauged without leaving its timetable?
faqs.a: Partly. Vehicle decks, voids, accessible ballast tanks and engine-room piping can be measured in timetable gaps or planned lay periods, provided the crew prepares the spaces and the car decks are empty. Bottom plating, sea chests and the remaining tanks are best measured in the annual docking. We divide the scope into packages so that each visit finishes its own spaces and nothing is left half-measured.

faqs.q: Can a superintendent in Mariehamn order gauging for a ship trading elsewhere?
faqs.a: Yes, and that suits Åland-managed ships well. Tell us the ship, its survey status and its next port or yard, and we plan the scope with the technical department, apply for whatever visa the destination requires and send the team to meet the ship there. Readings are reported on the class thickness measurement formats, so they can be used at the docking or survey wherever it takes place.

faqs.q: Where do Åland ferries go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: There is no merchant dry dock on the islands. Ferries on the Åland routes use mainland Finnish yards, such as Turku Repair Yard at Naantali and the shipyard at Rauma, as well as yards in Sweden, Poland and the Baltic states. Gauging done during service calls lets the owner send the yard measured steel quantities, and our team can also attend the docking to complete the programme.

faqs.q: Does Åland's special status change any survey or inspection rules?
faqs.a: Not for ship structure. Port state control in Mariehamn follows the Paris MoU as in the rest of Finland, and class and flag survey requirements are the same as for any ship. The special status matters commercially, because the tax border keeps ferries calling here, and that gives operators a strong reason to keep these ships on their routes and in sound structural condition.
